searchText: Thanks! Can you explain the difference between fixtures_stable and fixtures_develop please? I pulled in stable and still got Prague tests, which I wasn't expecting if develop is equivalent to pectra-devnet-6 release. <@892053833121923094> ☝️ this linked test violates EIP-7523: Empty accounts deprecation (it has empty account with non-empty storage in prestate), I think it should be removed or skipped from releases? Maybe better to send a PR with removal or replacement We agreed to activate this EIP right? https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4803 Does EEST ever do `t8n --state.reward -1`? seems like no. but I also wonder how genesis state is calculated for new prague The stable version should contain test fixtures for all forks up to Cancun, configured for all forks (up to Cancun)! For example: tests for Frontier configured only for Frontier, then all the Frontier & Homestead tests configured for Homestead..., up to the tests for all stable forks configured for Cancun! We'll aim to move Prague into stable after the hardfork 😄 I just tried pulling in stable and don't see Prague within it. Could you confirm that we have the same root hash within `v4.0.0/fixtures_stable/fixtures/.meta/index.json`: `0x969978e723a535333846fa0abeab3e9e96d7e0c21b6911e184015eb8de1271d` still not sure how that skip flag works It looks like it is only skipped for the `execute` command and not `fill` so it would show up in releases for this reason Pyspecs uses eels classes to calculate state root hash so it doesn't require a t8n call for that Thanks for the extra details. It was an issue on my end - our runner must have been caching some previous tests, it works as expected now 🙂 > We'll aim to move Prague into stable after the hardfork Will this be in another release, e.g. 4.1.0 or 5.0.0?

excerpts.author: spencer_tb
excerpts.content:
The stable version should contain test fixtures for all forks up to Cancun, configured for all forks (up to Cancun)! For example: tests for Frontier configured only for Frontier, then all the Frontier & Homestead tests configured for Homestead..., up to the tests for all stable forks configured for Cancun! We'll aim to move Prague into stable after the hardfork 😄

I just tried pulling in stable and don't see Prague within it. Could you confirm that we have the same root hash within `v4.0.0/fixtures_stable/fixtures/.meta/index.json`:
`0x969978e723a535333846fa0abeab3e9e96d7e0c21b6911e184015eb8de1271d`

excerpts.content: still not sure how that skip flag works

excerpts.author: spencer_tb
excerpts.content: It looks like it is only skipped for the `execute` command and not `fill` so it would show up in releases for this reason

excerpts.author: dimitry8570
excerpts.content: Pyspecs uses eels classes to calculate state root hash so it doesn't require a t8n call for that
